transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-12 14:00 PDT | Duration: 41m | Attendees: Alex Lopez (Redwood AE), Priya Reddy (Redwood SE), Jonah Park (Redwood Solutions); Maya Chen (BlueWave Lead ML), Evan Park (BlueWave CTO), Lucas Rivera (PM), Rita Gomez (SRE)

[00:00] Alex Lopez (Redwood AE): Hey, hey everybody, thanks for making time. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the results from the last week.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here.
[00:10] Evan Park: Evan on the call.
[00:12] Lucas Rivera: Lucas.
[00:13] Rita Gomez: Rita here.
[00:15] Priya Reddy (Redwood SE): Priya, hi. Jonah Park here as well.
[00:18] Alex Lopez: Awesome. So agenda: results review, SDK integration issues (function calling + structured output), perf tuning (batching / KV cache warm-up), and then actions. Priya, can you kick off with the SDK patch summary?
[00:28] Priya Reddy: Yeah, sure. So last week we saw two main failure modes when BlueWave used streaming + function_call to emit structured JSON: one was truncated JSON when clients consumed partial streams and tried to parse early, and the other was the model occasionally emitting non-conforming keys (like "user-id" vs "user_id"). We pushed a small SDK patch that a) forces model to use function_call with a strict JSON schema wrapper, b) buffers the stream until a complete JSON object is observed, and c) exposes a convenience validator. I posted the diff to the shared repo: shorturl.at/sdksnippet (link in meeting notes).
[01:05] Maya Chen: Quick question: when you say "buffer until complete JSON", does that add latency? In our QA runs we saw p95 go from ~170ms to ~260ms on a 512 token average turn.
[01:18] Priya Reddy: Good call out. The buffering adds a small micro-batching effect for streaming consumers, we measured median +20–80ms per response depending on when the first bytes arrive. But you get deterministic parseability. We can make buffering optional per-route.
[01:32] Evan Park: That tradeoff might be OK if it means no parse errors. Our FE team can't handle intermittent JSON errors.
[01:38] Lucas Rivera: Also, one thing we observed — the model sometimes emits additional debug text before the JSON payload, like "debug: trace id..." — any way to strip that reliably?
[01:46] Priya Reddy: The schema enforcement via function_call prevents that. We wrap expected output as a single function with arguments matching the JSON schema; the model returns a function invocation with exactly typed args. Even then, the stream can include noise if you're not using the function_call mode end-to-end.
[01:57] Maya Chen: Ok so we need full function_call end-to-end. We were mixing the raw text endpoint and the function wrapper in different calls, that might explain inconsistencies.
[02:03] Jonah Park: One more note: we added a helper in the SDK to auto-retry parse failures with a small jittered backoff and a 2nd attempt that pulls the full response from the non-streaming API as a fallback. It reduces customer-visible errors at the cost of extra tokens on rare failures.
[02:18] Rita Gomez: Token cost is a concern. Can you quantify how often that fallback triggers in your tests?
[02:22] Priya Reddy: In our canary it was ~0.7% of requests across mixed workloads. We estimated additional token bill of ~0.01–0.03% overall. Alex, I think you put together a cost sensitivity sheet?
[02:34] Alex Lopez: Yes — I updated the cost/latency sheet in Drive: drive.redwood/bluewave-poc-costs (link). For the current staging mix (avg 512 tokens per request, ~60k tokens/day), fallback would add roughly $2–8/day on hosted pricing assumptions. Dedicated pricing would change the marginals, we'll estimate both.
[02:54] Evan Park: That's acceptable if stability is improved.
[02:57] Maya Chen: We also ran the KV cache warm-up experiment. Results: on a cold model instance, first 50 requests had 1.8x latency and some token duplication. After warm-up to ~200 requests, p99 stabilized near expected. We saw similar behavior on 2 different model variants.
[03:14] Priya Reddy: Yep that's consistent. Two options: we can pre-warm using synthetic prefix requests at deployment, or adjust routing to prefer already-warm nodes for low-latency routes. For the POC, we recommend a small warm-up job at container startup.
[03:27] Lucas Rivera: Is there tooling to visualize which nodes are warm? Rita: for your SREs.
[03:31] Rita Gomez: We need node-level metrics exposed somewhere.
[03:33] Priya Reddy: Redwood Console exposes per-model per-node KV metrics, you can hook the tracing token. I'll send dashboard links.
[03:40] Alex Lopez: Quick reprioritization: primary P0 for you guys is structured output reliability; P1 is latency tuning for streaming; P2 is cost optimizations. Sound right?
[03:51] Evan Park: Yep, agree.
[03:53] Maya Chen: Agree.
[03:55] Priya Reddy: On structured output, the other engineering tweak we discussed was stronger schema enforcement at the API layer — if we see any deviation from the function signature, we drop and request model re-run automatically, and surface as a non-200 in the SDK so the app can choose fallback behavior. That can be toggled.
[04:12] Jonah Park: Also recommended is the use of deterministic generation params for function_call endpoints (temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0) when you expect strict schemas. That reduces hallucinations in keys and types.
[04:23] Maya Chen: We did notice weird casing and hyphenation; temperature 0 helped a lot in the reproducibility tests.
[04:29] Lucas Rivera: Can you show a quick snippet of the recommended Python SDK pattern?
[04:33] Priya Reddy: Sure I'm going to paste the gist verbally — apologies for the rough transcript: "with redwood.client(api_key) as c: resp = c.chat.create(model='rw-ghost-13b', messages=..., function_call={'name':'emit_event','arguments_schema':{'type':'object','properties':{'user_id':{'type':'string'}, 'event_type':{'type':'string'}}}}, stream=True) buffer = [] for chunk in resp.stream(): buffer.append(chunk) if looks_like_complete_json(buffer): parsed = json.loads(''.join(buffer)) handle(parsed) else: # fallback to non-streaming full response = c.chat.create(..., stream=False) parsed = json.loads(full_response)"
[05:20] Maya Chen: That helps. Two follow-ups: 1) can we get an example that shows how to validate against a JSON schema and raise a clear exception so our FE returns a 400 to clients? 2) any recommended patterns for webhooks when the model returns a function_call we want to execute asynchronously?
[05:34] Priya Reddy: For 1) yes — we'll add a validator utility in the patched SDK. For 2) recommended: accept the function_call payload server-side, persist a minimal execution record (id, args, timestamp), enqueue to your worker; Redwood can optionally sign the webhook payloads with HMAC. We'll add a short example repo.
[05:52] Rita Gomez: About security: we need to see SAML/SSO integration docs and audit log retention for Private deployment. Can you attach those to the next email?
[05:59] Alex Lopez: Yep — I'll attach SOC2 summary, SAML steps, and audit retention options.
[06:05] Evan Park: Anything else on perf? We tried increasing batching window and saw improved throughput but worse single-request latency.
[06:11] Priya Reddy: That's the classic throughput vs latency tradeoff. For user-facing low-latency routes keep batch window small (10–20ms) and use prefix caching aggressively. For background jobs you can push batch windows to 50–100ms. Also quantization profiles on dedicated hardware could reduce per-token cost with a modest latency impact.
[06:33] Maya Chen: For the immediate POC, we'll keep user routes low-latency and schedule heavier inference in a separate path.
[06:39] Alex Lopez: Great. Quick recap of who does what, then we'll wrap.
[06:43] Priya Reddy: Action items: I'll push the patched SDK example (Python) with schema validator and streaming buffer; I'll include a fallback example to non-streaming. Link + tiny repo.
[06:51] Maya Chen: I'll run 5k message regression and upload raw logs to the shared benchmark sheet (link: sheets.redwood/bluewave-poc-bench).
[06:58] Rita Gomez: I'll share the SRE access list for the Dedicated trial.
[07:02] Alex Lopez: I'll update the cost/latency breakouts and add the estimated delta for the fallback path.
[07:07] Lucas Rivera: Please also include example error payloads so our FE can map them to useful user messages.
[07:12] Priya Reddy: Yep will do.
[07:14] Alex Lopez: Ok, let's schedule a short mid-week check for Friday — 15 minutes to see progress on parsing errors. I'll send calendar invite. Any final questions?
[07:22] Evan Park: Not from me.
[07:24] Maya Chen: No.
[07:25] Alex Lopez: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: occasional transcription noise (e.g., "K V cash" instead of "KV cache"). Shared artifacts mentioned: drive.redwood/bluewave-poc-costs, sheets.redwood/bluewave-poc-bench, shorturl.at/sdksnippet.
